judge_comment: Directly targets the manual quote-comparison pain point with a reasonable time-saving estimate; it's distinct from the claims/risk-gap assistant, is document extraction with no worker evaluation or other Annex III activity so minimal risk is correct, and GDPR exposure is negligible given policy/broker data is mostly corporate rather than personal.

Directly addresses the need for insurance expertise and rushed timeline by analyzing claims/risk data rather than just extracting terms, so it complements rather than duplicates the document_extraction use case; minimal AI Act risk is correct since this is internal analytical support, not an Annex III category, though gdpr "none" is slightly understated given claims history may include personal/sensitive data.

Directly targets the condition-assessment pain point with agent-in-the-loop approval, complements rather than duplicates the order-history/eligibility assistant, and a 35% time saving plus minimal AI Act risk (not an Annex III category) are defensible, though "minimal" slightly understates typical EU AI Act transparency obligations for image-based automated assessment—still broadly correct.

Directly addresses the multi-system lookup pain point with a realistic time-saving estimate, does not overlap with the separate photo-condition classifier, and minimal risk classification is appropriate since this is a decision-support/retrieval tool rather than automated evaluation of persons.

Extraction/standardization is a distinct upstream step from the matching/triage classifier, so no overlap, and a 25% time saving plus minimal AI Act risk (document extraction, not an Annex III use case) is defensible.

Directly addresses the manual matching/triage pain point without overlapping the extraction use case, and minimal risk/indirect GDPR with a plausible 35% time saving are defensible since this is a finance back-office task, not an Annex III category.

Directly targets the core copy-paste pain point without overlapping the status-classification use case, and both the minimal AI Act risk and 35% time saving are plausible for this low-stakes content-scheduling task; GDPR 'none' is reasonable since content/marketing data is unlikely to involve personal data.
Directly targets the status-tracking pain point without duplicating the other use case's scheduling-form automation; minimal risk and modest time savings are plausible for a classification task.

Directly targets the severity-categorization pain point without overlapping the duplicate-detection assistant, and minimal risk classification is defensible since IT ticket severity is not an Annex III category, though 25% time saved is a touch optimistic for a classifier alone.

Directly targets the duplicate-detection and ownership-routing pain points without overlapping the severity classifier use case, and minimal AI Act risk is appropriate since IT ticket triage is not an Annex III category, though 20% time saved for an 8-minute task seems slightly high for a retrieval-assist tool.

Directly targets the core pain point of complex, error-prone rule application, but framing as a "classifier" is odd since this is deterministic rule-based logic better suited to a rules engine than ML, and 50% time savings seems optimistic given exception handling still needed; minimal AI Act risk is correct since commission tiering is not an Annex III category.

Directly targets the core pain point of manual compliance checking across disconnected channels, is complementary (not overlapping) with the downstream classification use case, and document extraction/validation of identity/right-to-work docs is reasonably classified as minimal risk (not an Annex III category) though GDPR sensitivity is correctly flagged; the 40% time saved is plausible for a 20-minute manual task.

This overlaps substantially with the document_extraction use case's "flags missing/incomplete documents" function, and since it gates IT system access and is part of the onboarding/recruitment process touching worker evaluation/eligibility, it arguably falls under Annex III (determining access to employment-related systems) rather than minimal risk; pct_time_saved of 25% is plausible but risk labeling is questionable.

Directly targets the inconsistent free-text pain point with a plausible extraction/standardization approach and reasonable time savings; this is a safety-logging tool not covered by Annex III categories, so minimal risk is defensible, and it does not overlap the separate corrective-action tracking use case.

Directly addresses the untracked corrective-action pain point and doesn't overlap the photo/text extraction use case, but this is essentially a simple rules-based status check (overdue vs. target date) that barely needs "AI" classification, making the 25% time savings and framing somewhat inflated; minimal AI Act risk is correctly assigned since this is safety/task tracking rather than worker evaluation.
